job.style: a puzzle or game that uses the idea

passage: Rohan is designing a rectangular garden game board where the area must be exactly 40 square units. He writes the equation x² - 3x = 40 to represent the dimensions. To solve this, he first rearranges it into the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, identifying a=1, b=-3, and c=-40. Rohan knows that for any quadratic equation, the discriminant D = b² - 4ac helps determine the nature of the roots. He calculates D = (-3)² - 4(1)(-40), which equals 9 + 160 = 169. Since 169 is greater than zero, he concludes there are two distinct real roots. He then factors the equation into (x - 8)(x + 5) = 0. He realizes that while x = 8 and x = -5 are both mathematical solutions to the equation, a physical length cannot be negative. Therefore, he rejects x = -5 and keeps x = 8 as the only valid dimension for his garden board. He checks his work by substituting 8 back into the original expression, confirming that 8² - 3(8) indeed equals 40. Rohan successfully avoids common traps, ensuring his quadratic model perfectly matches the physical reality of his game design.

items.evidence: To solve this, he first rearranges it into the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, identifying a=1, b=-3, and c=-40.
items.q: Rohan rewrites x² − 3x = 40 in standard form. What are a, b and c?
items.explain: Moving 40 to the left gives x² − 3x − 40 = 0, so c becomes −40.

wrong.why: reads c from the right side without moving it
drops the negative sign of b
takes a as the power 2 of x

items.evidence: Since 169 is greater than zero, he concludes there are two distinct real roots.
items.q: What does a discriminant of 169, greater than zero, tell Rohan?
options: There are two different real roots
There is one root, equal to 13
There is only one real root
There are no real roots at all
items.explain: A discriminant greater than zero means the equation has two distinct real roots.

wrong.why: thinks the root is the square root of a number
thinks a quadratic gives only one answer
mixes up positive and negative discriminant

items.evidence: He then factors the equation into (x - 8)(x + 5) = 0.
items.q: Rohan gets (x − 8)(x + 5) = 0. Which values of x solve it?
items.explain: Each factor is set to zero: x − 8 = 0 gives 8, x + 5 = 0 gives −5.

wrong.why: flips the sign of each factor's number
ignores the signs inside the brackets
sets each factor equal to 40 instead of 0

items.evidence: He realizes that while x = 8 and x = -5 are both mathematical solutions to the equation, a physical length cannot be negative.
items.q: Why does Rohan keep only x = 8 for his garden board?
options: A side of a board cannot be negative
Only x = 8 makes the equation true
A quadratic can have only one root
items.explain: Both 8 and −5 solve the equation, but a real length cannot be negative.

wrong.why: thinks −5 is not a solution of the equation
thinks a quadratic has only one answer
misreads the root from the factor's sign
